cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Test the Impossible Claim
cards.instruction: Get someone else to take the first practical step that could prove the bizarre claim true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. There's an invisible bridge across this ditch. Tap for it with your umbrella before I cross.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Yours extends. You can test it without leaving the bank.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll probe. But a surface isn't proof it'll hold you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Slide your picnic basket onto it first. Leave my lunch inside; I want a convincing weight.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs B to probe before A crosses, A3 rejects the tool swap through reach, and A5 orders B's basket onto the bridge.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 walking-stick alternative causes A3 extending umbrella reason; B4 load concern causes A5 weighted basket.

relationship.evidence: B2 questions why B must test and B4 correctly distinguishes surface from capacity.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 objection to add a practical load test while preserving B's first action.

specificity.evidence: A1 invisible bridge over ditch and B2 tools make the test understandable.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 leave my lunch in adds A's small stake to B4 weight requirement.
